About

I am a Senior Software Engineer with more than eight years of experience building and shipping software across a wide range of projects.

Originally from Nepal and now based in Texas, I hold a Master of Science in Computer Science and am currently pursuing graduate study in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence at Indiana Wesleyan University. Over the last few years my focus has shifted steadily toward AI — moving from simply using AI tools to understanding the fundamentals beneath them, so I can build solutions that are both technically sound and genuinely useful.

I care about the parts of engineering that are easy to skip: making a system understandable, designing for the person who actually has to use it, and being honest about what a tool can and cannot do. Outside of work and study, I spend my time at the gym, following the markets, and building side projects.

Portfolio Artifacts

Artifact 01 · AIML-500

ML Study Buddy — An AI Tutor for Machine Learning Fundamentals

A working, conversational AI assistant that helps students new to AI and machine learning understand core concepts in plain language and check their own understanding — built end to end using a design-thinking process.

Objective

To give students who are new to AI/ML a patient, judgment-free way to understand core concepts and quiz themselves, available any time — without having the tool do their graded work for them.

Process

I applied the five phases of design thinking — empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test. After identifying the real pain point (beginners overwhelmed by jargon), I planned the assistant's objective, scope, guardrails, and tone, then prototyped and iterated it against test scenarios until it reliably explained concepts, checked understanding, and declined to do graded work.

Tools & Technologies

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for a self-contained web application; a large language model to generate responses; and design-thinking methodology to guide the build. Full tutor instructions and guardrails were written directly into the system prompt.

Description

A single-page chat application with a warm tutor persona. It explains a concept simply, gives an analogy or example, and ends by checking the student's understanding. It is built to stay on-topic, flag uncertainty, protect privacy by storing no conversation, and refuse to produce submittable work.

Value Proposition

Unique value: Most AI chat tools will happily do a student's work for them. ML Study Buddy is deliberately the opposite — it is engineered to teach and quiz rather than to answer, which protects learning instead of short-circuiting it. Relevance: It shows I can take a real human need, apply a structured design process, and ship a working, responsible AI product — not just describe one.

Artifact 02 · AIML-500

The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence — A Visual Timeline

A researched, designed timeline that traces seven decades of AI history — its milestones, its two "AI winters," and the deep-learning breakthroughs — in a single visual a non-expert can follow at a glance.

Objective

To take the dense, technical history of AI and communicate it clearly and visually, so that the pattern of hype, setback, and breakthrough is easy to understand for any audience.

Process

I researched and verified key milestones across seven decades, grouped them into four eras, and designed a color-coded vertical timeline that makes the rhythm of progress and setback visible at a glance.

Tools & Technologies

Research and synthesis, information and data design, and HTML and CSS for layout, rendered to a high-resolution graphic. I used ChatGPT to help gather and verify the milestones, then designed and wrote the timeline myself.

Description

A vertical, color-coded timeline covering four eras — Foundations, the AI Winters, Expert Systems, and the Deep Learning Revolution — with the key figures and companies behind each milestone.

Value Proposition

Unique value: This shows a different strength than my first artifact. Where the chatbot proves I can build a working product, this timeline proves I can take something dense and technical and make it clear, visual, and genuinely teachable. Relevance: In AI and ML work, explaining complex ideas to non-technical stakeholders is as valuable as the engineering itself, and this artifact demonstrates that communication skill directly.

More artifacts to come. Additional projects from AIML-500 will be added here as the course continues, each documented with its objective, process, tools, and value.
